question: What will be the average daily mean temperature in Cape Town over the 7 days ending October 14, 2026, in degrees Celsius?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the mean of the daily mean 2-metre air temperatures from 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-14 at latitude -33.92, longitude 18.42 (Cape Town), from the ERA5 reanalysis as served by the Open-Meteo historical weather API (archive-api.open-meteo.com), in degrees Celsius.
research:
The ERA5 value for 8 to 14 October 2026 is not in yet, since the window opens on 8 October, so nothing has settled the question. Over 2019 to 2025 that same week averaged about 15.2 to 18.0 °C, mean about 16.6 °C. September 2026 has been running warmer than the last four years so far.

### 1. Resolution source
- The Open-Meteo archive API, asked for latitude -33.92 and longitude 18.42, returns data for the nearest grid cell at **-33.99, 18.43**. That cell sits slightly south of the city centre and is affected by the sea. I queried it with GMT timezone, which is the default; the question does not say which timezone to use. [Open-Meteo](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2026-08-15&end_date=2026-09-15&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT)
- 2026-09-15: the latest value shown is a daily mean of **14.4 °C**. From 9 to 15 September the values were 17.4, 16.8, 17.2, 16.4, 17.6, 14.8 and 14.4 °C. [Open-Meteo](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2026-08-15&end_date=2026-09-15&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The resolution window starts in about 3 weeks, beyond the useful range of daily weather forecasts.
- 2026-09-01 to 09-15: the mean was **16.8 °C**. A warm spell peaked on 7 September at 22.1 °C, with daily values of 20.6, 22.1 and 20.5 °C from 6 to 8 September. [Open-Meteo](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2026-08-15&end_date=2026-09-15&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT)

### 3. Recent news
- 2026-09-13/14: the South African Weather Service (SAWS) issued a Yellow Level 4 warning for disruptive rain from a cut-off low in parts of the Western Cape and Northern Cape. The ERA5 daily means then fell to about 14.4 to 14.8 °C. [SAnews](https://www.sanews.gov.za/node/84268)
- 2026-09-09: Citizen forecast: "cool to warm" weather with fire danger in the Western Cape. [Citizen](https://citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/weather/weather-forecast-9-september-2026)
- 2026-09-02: a SAWS seasonal outlook for September 2026 to January 2027, as reported in the press, points to a hotter-than-normal summer and a strengthening El Niño. The coverage gave nothing specific to the Western Cape. [ATC News](https://atcnews.org/travelcomments-com-south-africas-summer-weather-outlook-hotter-and-drier-conditions-expected/)
- 2026-04-08: forecasts were leaning drier for the winter-rainfall region. [Daily Maverick](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-04-08-latest-forecast-for-sas-winter-rainfall-regions-shifts-to-drier-gear-)

### 4. Base rates
The figures below are the 8 to 14 October means from the same API and grid cell, which I calculated from the daily values:

| Year | Mean, 8 to 14 Oct (°C) | Daily range (°C) |
|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 16.57 | 14.0 to 19.8 |
| 2020 | 15.21 | 13.3 to 17.8 |
| 2021 | 16.73 | 13.9 to 19.8 |
| 2022 | 18.00 | 16.4 to 22.1 |
| 2023 | 16.49 | 14.3 to 19.2 |
| 2024 | 16.06 | 14.3 to 19.0 |
| 2025 | 17.34 | 15.5 to 19.3 |

- Across these 7 years the mean is about **16.6 °C** and the spread is about ±0.9 °C (1 SD), with a full range of 15.2 to 18.0 °C. There is no clear trend.
- Individual days in early to mid October can reach 19 to 24 °C during berg-wind (hot offshore wind) events. For example, 4 October 2024 hit 24.4 °C. These spikes can push a 7-day mean up by about 1 °C.

**How the season moves from mid-September to mid-October:**

| Year | Mean, 10 to 15 Sep (°C) | Mean, 8 to 14 Oct (°C) | Change (°C) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 15.07 | 18.00 | +2.9 |
| 2023 | 12.2 | 16.49 | +4.3 |
| 2024 | 13.3 | 16.06 | +2.8 |
| 2025 | 15.1 | 17.34 | +2.2 |
| 2026 | **16.2** | ? | ? |

- 2026 is running about 1 to 4 °C above the same September dates in 2022 to 2025. Over 2022 to 2025, a year's mid-September level did not reliably predict its October value: 2023 was the coldest in September but sat mid-pack in October.
- Sources: [2022](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2022-09-10&end_date=2022-10-14&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT), [2023](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2023-09-10&end_date=2023-10-14&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT), [2024](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2024-09-10&end_date=2024-10-14&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT), [2025](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2025-09-10&end_date=2025-10-14&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT), [2021](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2021-10-01&end_date=2021-10-20&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT), [2020](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2020-10-08&end_date=2020-10-14&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT), [2019](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.92&longitude=18.42&start_date=2019-10-08&end_date=2019-10-14&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=GMT)

### 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market, or any expert forecast, on this question or a close variant.

### 6. Upcoming events and outlook
- 8 to 14 October will only come within the range of deterministic and ensemble forecasts in late September and early October. Nothing reliable is available as of today.
- 2026-09-02: SAWS's September 2026 to January 2027 outlook, as reported, leans hotter than normal nationally, with El Niño strengthening. I could not find a temperature outlook specific to the Western Cape or Cape Town; the official Seasonal Climate Watch PDF on the SAWS site would be the place to check. [ATC News](https://atcnews.org/travelcomments-com-south-africas-summer-weather-outlook-hotter-and-drier-conditions-expected/)
- Two weather patterns matter most for the outcome: berg-wind events, which raise temperatures, and cold fronts or cut-off lows, which lower them.
